body.statement: For every \(n\ge1\), every \(0<\alpha<1\), every design \(B\), and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}\), the projected set \(\mathcal C_n\) satisfies \(\Pr_P\{Q(P)\in\mathcal C_n\}\ge1-\alpha\). Its coordinate extrema are finite constrained polynomial optimization problems after closure, because \(\Phi_{T,S,B,e}\) is polynomial in the finite primitive tables with known \(e\).
body.justification: Projection supplies honest finite-sample coverage on singular and nonidentified strata without upgrading generic optimization into the headline identification algorithm.
body.gap: Existing smooth double-sampling intervals do not cover rank-changing or nonidentified partial-audit laws; Duarte et al. supply the adjacent polynomial-program representation rather than this design-specific cube projection.
body.consumer: Studies whose chosen bundle is insufficient, or whose data lie near a singular branch, still obtain globally valid uncertainty sets for endpoint intervention probabilities.
